data.title: Middle East Eye: Somali-American Uber driver left in coma after alleged hate crime in Minnesota
data.author: MEE staff
data.summary:
Somali-American Uber driver left in coma after alleged hate crime in Minnesota
Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Mon, 11/16/2026 - 18:46
Mohamed Yusuf was reportedly run over multiple times with his own vehicle after a passenger said he disliked his Muslim name
A screenshot of a GoFundMe fundraiser launched to support Mohamed Yusuf, the Somali-American Uber driver who was the victim of a suspected hate crime in Minnesota
Off
A Somali-American Uber driver is fighting for his life after being strangled and repeatedly run over with his own vehicle, allegedly by a passenger in Minnesota, in an attack his family believes was motivated by anti-Muslim hatred.
Mohamed Yusuf was working in Hopkins, a suburb of Minneapolis, early on Saturday when a passenger allegedly asked him his name before telling him he did not like the name "Mohamed".
According to Yusuf's relatives, the passenger then allegedly choked him from behind, seized control of his vehicle and ran him over multiple times.
"He was run over multiple times with his own vehicle," Yusuf's son, Mustafa Osman, told The Somali Brief.
Yusuf was reportedly found in a ditch nearly a mile away, suffering from broken legs and ribs, two collapsed lungs, a spinal injury and internal bleeding.
He remains hospitalised in a coma, according to his family.
Hopkins police confirmed that officers responding to a report of a suspicious vehicle at around 1.20am on Saturday discovered a seriously injured man and subsequently took a male suspect into custody.
According to the Times of India, arrest records show that a man identified as Samit Apurva Patel was taken into custody by Hopkins Police on 14 November on a first-degree assault charge.
However, authorities have not confirmed whether Patel's arrest is connected to Yusuf's assault or publicly identified the suspect in the case.
Police have also not established a motive or confirmed whether the incident is being investigated as a hate crime.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Iran still retains up to 2,500 ballistic missiles: Report
data.author: Hossam Desouky
data.summary:
Iran still retains up to 2,500 ballistic missiles: Report
The US believes Iran has between 1,500 and 2,500 ballistic missiles in its arsenal, a substantial number that contradicts the Trump administration’s claims that Iran has been militarily decimated.
The US intelligence community ranked the assessment “low confidence”, The Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, but the American estimate generally aligns with Israel’s, which says Iran has more than 1,500 missiles.
President Donald Trump has regularly characterised Iran as a defeated and broken nation. Full-scale war between the US and Iran has subsided, but the two are still exchanging strikes.
Iran attacked US military assets in Bahrain twice in the last week in response to US strikes on its own military infrastructure. Iran also said on Monday that it struck two vessels in the Strait of Hormuz with mines, sinking one Very Large Crude Carrier, known as a VLCC.
The fact that Iran retains a vast arsenal of ballistic missiles may be why the US has refrained from relaunching strikes on Iran, despite Trump boasting that the US had “won” the war and achieved a “93 percent victory” over the Islamic Republic.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Mamdani to disband special NYPD unit deployed during pro-Palestinian protests
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Mamdani to disband special NYPD unit deployed during pro-Palestinian protests
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced on Monday that he will keep his campaign promise to disband the New York Police Department's Strategic Response Group (SRG) and replace it with “de-escalation groups”.
The armour-clad SRG is made up of 500 highly trained NYPD officers who have become infamous for their “crowd control tactics” and mass arrests during protests in New York City, where they use batons, tear gas, pepper spray and other “de-escalation” weapons on disruptive protesters.
The group came under particular scrutiny during pro-Palestine protests during the height of Israel’s genocide in Gaza and campus protests led by the student movement that started at Columbia University.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Indian minister confirms no casualties onboard tanker hit by missile in Hormuz Strait
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Indian minister confirms no casualties onboard tanker hit by missile in Hormuz Strait
India’s Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal announced that there were no casualties following a missile strike on a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz.
The Panama-flagged liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) tanker Tara Gas was carrying 24 Indian sailors at the time.
"All 24 Indian nationals, along with the entire 25-member crew, are completely safe with no injuries," Sonowal said in a post on X.
"We are continuously monitoring the situation and remain in close contact with the ship management company to ensure the ongoing security and wellbeing of our seafarers."

Iran’s top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has warned retaliation to the US and Israel after a New York Times report quoted analysts suggesting Tehran's "dual-use" of civilian infrastructure.
"Prepping the next round on civilian infra, their 'experts' tell NYT: 'dams near Iran’s missile sites are dual-use.'," he mockingly referenced the article.
"Cool. New rule: Any dam, port, or power plant near a US or Israeli base is dual-use. We’ll apply your logic consistently and even-handedly," Ghalibaf added.
The US and Israel have previously attacked civilian areas and infrastructure across the region under the guise that they are used for military purpose, despite having no backing for such claims.
As a result, countless civilians have been killed and wounded in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.
